text:
Alex M: FYI customer (acme) reporting repeated 401s after rotating their API key. They say the old key stopped working (good) but new key returns 401 from our Python SDK in their long-running worker processes.

Alex M: Paste of error they sent:
```
HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 953, in raise_for_status
    raise HTTPError(http_error_msg, response=self)
  File "/app/worker/run.py", line 42, in process_job
    resp = client.generate(prompt)
```

Alex M: They say they set env vars in the host before restart: REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG. Worker is a long-lived process that reloads job configs but not restarted during key rotation.

Mira S: Do we know SDK version? Any chance of pinned older version that caches auth?

Alex M: Customer is on redwood-sdk 0.9.2. They also sent our SDK debug logs (redacted):
```
[redwood.sdk] DEBUG Sending request to /v1/generate
[redwood.sdk] DEBUG Headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_live_OLDKEY', 'Redwood-Org': None, 'User-Agent': 'redwood-python/0.9.2'}
[redwood.sdk] DEBUG Response status: 401
```

Alex M: Note: headers show 'Redwood-Org': None even though REDWOOD_ORG was set in env. If they restart the worker it picks up new key and works. So seems like old key value persisted.

Chris K: Sounds like two separate issues: (1) API key rotation for running processes, (2) env var reading for org/project headers returning None. We should repro locally.

Mira S: Repro steps request to customer: can you confirm you do NOT call Client(api_key=...) at process start with old key? Also confirm you rely on env var only.

Alex M: Customer replied: they call Client() with no args, relying on env var. They set REDWOOD_API_KEY to new key in the environment and sent a signal SIGHUP to reload config (their code watches for changes and reloads app config but does not create a new Client).

Mira S: That fits: our SDK 0.9.2 caches credential at import/client init. If they never reinstantiate Client, worker uses cached token. Workaround: recreate client after rotation, or call client.update_auth(new_key) if available.

Chris K: I pulled the code: in 0.9.2 Client loads env var at module import and stores it on a module-global _DEFAULT_AUTH. Also Redwood-Org header getter does os.getenv('REDWOOD_ORG') at import time in that release, so if env var was empty at startup it becomes None permanently. That's a bug.

Mira S: Ok short-term workaround we can recommend to customer: (a) restart the worker (b) instantiate a new Client() after rotation (c) set explicit api_key when creating client: Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']). Example we can paste: 
```python
# safe pattern for long-running processes
import os
from redwood import Client

def get_client():
    return Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), org=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_ORG'))

# call get_client() inside the job loop so a fresh client is used after rotation
```

Alex M: Customer tried explicit Client(api_key=...) and that fixed it immediately. They applied as temporary fix.

Mira S: Good. Medium-term: we should patch SDK to lazily read env vars on client creation and expose a method to rotate keys at runtime, plus a changelog note. Chris, can you triage a bug?

Chris K: Filed GH issue and draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/789 (internal link). Fix does two things: read env vars during Client.__init__ instead of module import, and add Client.reload_auth(new_api_key=None) to atomically update Authorization and org/project headers. Unit tests added for rotation and header population. Target patch release 0.9.3.

Alex M: Created support ticket for the customer and linked the PR: TKT-4521. Notified customer about workaround and planned patch. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket TKT-4521 created and linked to GH PR 789. ETA for patch release 0.9.3: 48-72h.

Mira S: For docs: add a Recipe in DevEx 'Key rotation in long-running processes' showing get_client pattern and mention the env var names REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ORG, REDWOOD_PROJECT and explicit Client args. Also callout that old SDK <=0.9.2 reads env at import time.

Chris K: Quick commands for customers who can pip-upgrade:
```bash
pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk==0.9.3  # when released
# or immediate fallback: recreate client with explicit api key in code
```

Alex M: I'll follow up with the customer once 0.9.3 is out. Adding note to ticket: "customer uses long-running workers; recommended pattern: don't rely on import-time env caching; recreate client or upgrade."

Mira S: Thanks. Marking as escalation resolved for support channel pending release.

Chris K: I'll merge PR once CI green, will ping here with release tag.

Alex M: ACK.
